title: Case #8: The Slow Dashboard
summary: Teodor wants a bigger server. Profile the queries, fix them, and find the deploy that broke everything.

steps.title: Case #8
body: Teodor's dashboard has gone from 2 seconds to **11**. He has a quote for a server three times the size. Rosa asks for one day first.
You have the app's **query log** (each query's calls per page load and average time), the dashboard's daily **p95 latency** (95% of loads are faster than this), and the **deploy** history.

steps.title: Clue 1: where the time goes
prompt: Return each **query_name** with its total time per page load (**ms_per_page** = calls_per_page × avg_ms), biggest first.

Tables: `stations(id, name, district)` (40 rows) and `rides(id, rider_id, station_id, started, minutes, fare_cents)` (20,000 rows; `started` is text like `'2026-03-14 08:05:00'`). Also `query_log(query_name, feature, calls_per_page, avg_ms)`, `dashboard_latency(day, p95_ms)` and `deploys(id, day, author, feature)`.
solution: SELECT query_name, calls_per_page * avg_ms AS ms_per_page
setup: PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;
CREATE TABLE stations (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, district TEXT NOT NULL);

WITH RECURSIVE n(i) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT i + 1 FROM n WHERE i < 40) INSERT INTO stations SELECT i, 'Station ' || i, CASE i % 4 WHEN 0 THEN 'Docklands' WHEN 1 THEN 'Old Town' WHEN 2 THEN 'Northside' ELSE 'Harbourside' END FROM n;

CREATE TABLE rides (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, rider_id INTEGER NOT NULL, station_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES stations(id), started TEXT NOT NULL, minutes INTEGER NOT NULL, fare_cents INTEGER NOT NULL);

WITH RECURSIVE n(i) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT i + 1 FROM n WHERE i < 20000) INSERT INTO rides SELECT i, (i * 7919) % 500 + 1, (i * 31) % 40 + 1, datetime('2026-01-01', '+' || ((i * 7) % 300) || ' days', '+' || ((i * 13) % 1440) || ' minutes'), (i * 37) % 55 + 2, ((i * 37) % 55 + 2) * 15 FROM n;
CREATE TABLE query_log (query_name TEXT PRIMARY KEY, feature TEXT, calls_per_page INTEGER, avg_ms INTEGER);

INSERT INTO query_log VALUES ('kpi_tiles','kpis',1,90),('monthly_revenue','reports',1,1800),('station_name_lookup','recent-activity',2000,4),('login_check','auth',1,3),('rider_count','kpis',1,140),('weather_widget','weather',1,250);
CREATE TABLE dashboard_latency (day TEXT PRIMARY KEY, p95_ms INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE deploys (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, day TEXT, author TEXT, feature TEXT);

INSERT INTO deploys VALUES (1,'2026-11-02','Kit Brannagh','weather'),(2,'2026-11-04','Ola Nwosu','kpis'),(3,'2026-11-06','Dane Ruiz','recent-activity'),(4,'2026-11-08','Kit Brannagh','auth'),(5,'2026-11-09','Ola Nwosu','reports');
steps.explain: `station_name_lookup` costs 8 seconds a page: a 4 ms query run **2,000 times**. Classic N+1. `monthly_revenue` is second at 1.8 seconds.

steps.title: Fix 3: kill the N+1
prompt: The recent-activity panel loads the **2,000** most recent rides, then looks up each one's station name separately. Replace it with one query returning **id**, **started** and station **name** for the **2,000 most recent** rides, newest first, ties broken by id descending.

Tables: `stations(id, name, district)` (40 rows) and `rides(id, rider_id, station_id, started, minutes, fare_cents)` (20,000 rows; `started` is text like `'2026-03-14 08:05:00'`). Also `query_log(query_name, feature, calls_per_page, avg_ms)`, `dashboard_latency(day, p95_ms)` and `deploys(id, day, author, feature)`.
solution: JOIN stations AS s ON s.id = r.station_id
ORDER BY r.started DESC, r.id DESC

steps.title: Name the culprit
prompt: When did it break, and who shipped it? Find the day the dashboard's p95 **jumped the most** from the previous day (use LAG), and return the **author** and **feature** of the deploy made **that day**.

Tables: `stations(id, name, district)` (40 rows) and `rides(id, rider_id, station_id, started, minutes, fare_cents)` (20,000 rows; `started` is text like `'2026-03-14 08:05:00'`). Also `query_log(query_name, feature, calls_per_page, avg_ms)`, `dashboard_latency(day, p95_ms)` and `deploys(id, day, author, feature)`.
solution: SELECT day, p95_ms - LAG(p95_ms) OVER (ORDER BY day) AS jump
SELECT day FROM jumps ORDER BY jump DESC LIMIT 1
JOIN worst AS w ON w.day = d.day;

Take the biggest jump's day, then join deploys on day.
steps.explain: **Dane Ruiz** shipped *recent-activity* on November 6th, and p95 went from 2.4 to 10.9 seconds the same day. It's the same feature as the N+1 query. No new server needed: one join and one index, and Teodor's dashboard is back under two seconds.
